sentences.text:
1 Appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 assailing the impugned award dated 9/8/2019 passed by Member, Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena in Claim Case No. 739/2017; whereby, learned Claims Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs. 5,57,552/- to the claimant/respondent No. 1 for the injuries sustained by him in road accident dated 6/2/2017.
2. Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 6/2/2017 when respondent No. 1/claimant was going on his motorcycle bearing No. MP06S0673, it is alleged that as soon as they reached Chaina Road Canal Bridge, a Loading vehicle bearing registration No. RJ11GA0185 being driven by its driver/respondent No. 3, dashed the motorcycle, due to which claimant suffered previous hurts in right leg, head and other parts of the body, therefore, he filed a claim case under Section 166 of MVA claiming total compensation of Rs. 72,00,000/-; however, by the impugned award, Claims Tribunal awarded a total compensation of RS. 5,57,552/- alongwith interest at the rate of 6% per annum and in lieu of delay in payment of compensation amount with penal interest @ 9% per annum in case of failure of Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

entities.text: Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Insurance Company mainly assailed the impugned award on the ground of false involvement of offending vehicle as accordingly to learned counsel for the Company, the FIR was lodged with a delay of 20 days and Claims Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact that as per document Ex. P/47, the doctor had written that the attender of the patient says that 'road traffic accident' by running bike on 6/2/2017 at 3. pm head injury.

It is further submitted that learned Claims Tribunal further erred in awarding Rs. 50,000/- separately under the head loss of happiness, services due to permanent disablement; whereas, while under the head loss of earning capacity, the Claims Tribunal had already awarded a sum of Rs. 3,00,240/- while calculating permanent disability to the extent of 20%
and therefore, said amount is liable to be deducted.
4.
learned counsel for the Claimant/respondent No. 1 supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

As regards contention of learned counsel for the appellant/Company that offending loading vehicles has been falsely involved in the matter just to claim compensation is concerned, all the objections raised by Insurance Company have been dealt within in detail by the claims Tribunal while deciding issue No. 1 para 6 to 19 of impugned award and a bare reading of such paragraphs,
makes it clear that learned Claims Tribunal did not err while overruling the objections raised by Insurance Company and this Court is fully in agreement with the same and therefore, such contentions of Insurance Company is hereby discarded.
7.

As regards second contention of learned counsel for the Insurance Company is concerned, from perusal of para 35 and 36 of the impugned award, it is clear that learned Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs. 50,000/- separately to the claimant under the head loss of happiness and services due to permanent disablement, whereas, while calculating the amount of compensation under the head Tata Aig General Insurance Company Thr. vs Pawan on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158434978/
2 loss of earning capacity, learned Claims Tribunal had already assessed the same @20% and thereafter calculated the amount, therefore, in the opinion of this Court, award of Rs. 50,000/-
separately under the head loss of happiness and services due to permanent disablement is bad in law and same is therefore, liable to be deducted and accordingly hereby deducted and instead of Rs.
5,57,552/-, respondent No. 1/claimant is held entitled to receive a total compensation of Rs.
5,07,552/- with interest @6% per annum from the date of claim application.
8.

As regards grant of penal interest in case of failure by Insurance Company to pay the compensation amount in the given time is concerned, in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Keshav Bahadur and Ors., (2004)1ACJ648 same cannot be done and accordingly, the findings of Claims Tribunal so far as imposition of penal interest is concerned, is hereby set aside.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Keshav Bahadur and Ors., (2004)1ACJ648 same
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. With the aforesaid modification in the impugned award, appeal is allowed in part.
Parties to bear their own cost.

(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
